questions.q: In the course, the underlay answers which question?
choices: Which SGT to assign a user
Which tenant or VRF should handle the packet after it arrives
How sites reach each other and which path traffic takes through the network
questions.why: The underlay is reachability and path. The overlay decides tenant, VRF, or service once the packet is at the far edge.

questions.q: A Layer 2 VPN service makes the provider network look like what to the enterprise?
choices: A logical router that exchanges BGP routes
questions.why: Layer 2 VPNs extend Ethernet. Layer 3 VPNs make the underlay look like a logical router.

questions.q: E-Line, pseudowire, and VPWS are provider terms for which design?
questions.why: Point-to-point Layer 2 uses those names. VPLS, EVPN, and E-LAN describe multipoint Layer 2.

questions.q: Why does the course pair GRE with IPsec for classic site-to-site routing?
choices: IPsec secures the traffic but does not carry multicast and broadcasts that routing protocols need
questions.why: The VPN slide says IPsec does not support multicast or broadcasts, which breaks routing protocols unless GRE is added.

questions.q: Which classic VPN fits a large branch design that needs dynamic spoke-to-spoke tunnels over the Internet?
choices: A manually configured tunnel per pair of sites
questions.why: The best-fit table maps DMVPN to branch hub-and-spoke with dynamic spoke-to-spoke tunnels. Manual tunnels fit a few static sites.

questions.q: GETVPN is the best fit when the customer needs what?
choices: Group encryption on an existing private WAN without building an overlay, while preserving the original IP header
A brand-new public Internet overlay for three sites
questions.why: GETVPN uses group IPsec, does not build an overlay, and keeps the IP header, which helps QoS, traffic engineering, and multicast.

questions.q: FlexVPN is distinguished in the deck by which trait?
choices: Tunnel-less encryption that preserves the original header on MPLS
One IKEv2 framework for site-to-site, hub-and-spoke, and spoke-to-spoke
A single static tunnel with no routing
questions.why: FlexVPN is the modern IKEv2 framework for several topologies. GETVPN is the tunnel-less private-WAN option.

questions.q: What does a VRF give a provider or a large enterprise?
choices: A separate routing table so customers or segments can overlap addresses and stay isolated
A shared global table for every customer
questions.why: Each VRF acts as its own Layer 3 network. The same prefixes can exist in different VRFs without conflict.

questions.q: On an MPLS path, a P router forwards a packet based on what?
choices: The MPLS label, without inspecting the IP header
questions.why: The MPLS header slide says the P router uses the label. PE routers impose and dispose of labels at the edge.

questions.q: Why might an enterprise that already owns its WAN still use MPLS?
choices: Because Internet DIA cannot carry IP
Control, deterministic latency, security and compliance, and legacy OT integration
Because VRFs do not work on private fiber
Because MPLS is required for every SaaS application
questions.why: The discussion answer lists control and independence, latency and determinism, security and compliance, and legacy OT.

questions.q: SD-WAN, as defined in the course, changes the WAN by doing what?
choices: Decoupling the data, control, and management planes and steering applications over multiple transports with centralized policy
Forcing every flow through one static route
questions.why: The definition is an SDN-style WAN: separated planes, a secure overlay, and application steering from centralized policy.

questions.q: In the Catalyst SD-WAN picture, which component is the management plane?
questions.why: Manager is the single pane for day-0, day-1, and day-2. Controllers distribute control and policy. The validator is the first authentication point. Edges forward data.

questions.q: OMP runs in which role?
choices: A TCP control protocol between WAN Edges and Controllers, inside authenticated TLS or DTLS
The data-plane cipher that encrypts user packets
A Layer 2 discovery protocol on the LAN
questions.why: OMP advertises routes, TLOCs, and policy between edges and controllers and between controllers, inside TLS or DTLS.

questions.q: How does Catalyst SD-WAN keep segments separate on the data plane?
choices: Segmentation requires the underlay to understand every VLAN
Guest traffic is sent in the clear
All users share one global routing table
Each VPN or VRF keeps its own table, and packets carry a label inside IPsec
questions.why: The data-plane slide shows per-VPN tables and an IPsec packet with a label so segmentation does not depend on the underlay.

questions.q: Application-aware routing chooses a path using which kind of information?
choices: The alphabetical order of provider names
Measured loss, latency, and jitter against an application SLA
questions.why: The example compares paths such as 10 ms and 1 percent loss versus 200 ms and 3 percent loss, then pins the application to a compliant path.

questions.q: Zero-touch provisioning for an SD-WAN edge uses which onboarding path?
choices: DHCP and DNS from the ISP to reach the PnP server, then an automatic join to the fabric
An on-site USB image with no certificates
A technician pasting a full configuration at every site
A manual GRE tunnel built before the device boots
questions.why: The ZTP example uses PnP, ISP DHCP and DNS, and then secure bring-up into the IPsec fabric.

questions.q: Multi-Region Fabric is used to do what?
choices: Group sites, such as by geography, and restrict overlay tunnels between regions
Replace IPsec with MACsec on the LAN
Stretch one VLAN across every country
questions.why: MRF lets you define regions, keep topologies different per region, and avoid a full mesh of overlay tunnels between distant sites.

questions.q: Why might a customer keep MPLS after deploying SD-WAN?
choices: MPLS can still offer predictable performance, an SLA, and low latency for traffic that needs it
Internet circuits are illegal for enterprise use
SD-WAN cannot forward traffic unless MPLS is present
questions.why: The transport-strategy answer says MPLS may remain for predictability and SLAs. Internet is often enough for general SaaS, and cellular fits rapid or backup sites.

questions.q: Cloud onRamp for SaaS at a remote site improves Office 365 or Webex by doing what?
choices: Disabling TLS so the path looks faster
Backhauling all SaaS through the data center by policy
Probing application quality out of each local Internet exit and steering to the better path
questions.why: The DIA onRamp example probes selected SaaS applications on each local exit and uses the better-performing circuit.

questions.q: On-box SD-WAN security called out in the module includes which set?
choices: URL filtering, Cisco Umbrella, and Advanced Malware Protection with file reputation
questions.why: The on-box security slide lists URL categories and reputation, Umbrella, and AMP with reputation and sandboxing.

questions.q: Which component is present in a Catalyst SD-WAN deployment and absent from SD-Routing?
questions.why: The architecture comparison shows Manager and Validator in both, and states that the SD-WAN Controller is not included for SD-Routing.

questions.q: SD-Routing is aimed at which customer?
choices: A customer who wants to keep DMVPN, FlexVPN, GETVPN, or MPLS VPN and add centralized management
A customer replacing the campus with BGP-EVPN
A customer who only needs OpenRoaming
A customer who already needs a full SD-WAN overlay and application-aware steering
questions.why: SD-Routing keeps classic routed VPNs and adds Manager-based operations without forcing an SD-WAN migration.

questions.q: A customer already on SD-WAN wants the same operational model for remaining Internet-edge routers. What does the customer-journey answer recommend?
choices: Rip out SD-WAN and return to static tunnels
Keep SD-WAN and bring the remaining devices under the same centralized management
Move those routers to GEO satellite only
questions.why: Customer A stays on SD-WAN and extends the same management to devices that are not yet in the fabric.

questions.q: Segment Routing chooses a path in which way?
choices: The destination rewrites the path at every hop
The source encodes an ordered list of segments in the packet
A SPAN port copies the packet to a controller for each hop
Every router independently floods a full traffic-engineering database and picks the next hop with no source instruction
questions.why: Segment Routing is source routing. Segments are instructions, such as a node or an adjacency, carried in the header.

questions.q: A Node-SID differs from an Adj-SID because a Node-SID does what?
choices: Identifies a router in the network, while an Adj-SID identifies a local link on that router
Identifies a VLAN on an access port
Replaces the need for any IGP
questions.why: Each node has a unique Node-SID. An Adj-SID has local significance for a link. Combining them steers traffic onto a specific path.

questions.q: Topology Independent LFA in the Segment Routing section is meant to provide what?
choices: About 50 ms protection for links, nodes, and shared-risk groups without waiting for full IGP convergence
questions.why: TI-LFA is the fast-reroute mechanism described as 100 percent coverage and 50-millisecond protection.

questions.q: SR-MPLS and SRv6 are which pair?
choices: A firewall mode and an IPS mode
A wireless deployment and a satellite orbit
Two data-plane ways to carry the same Segment Routing instructions, one with MPLS labels and one with IPv6 addresses
questions.why: The course presents one architecture with two instantiations: SID as an MPLS label, or SID as an IPv6 prefix.

questions.q: What operational problem does Segment Routing claim to reduce in a traditional MPLS core?
choices: The number of protocols needed for transport, VPNs, and traffic engineering
questions.why: The evolution slides collapse LDP, RSVP-TE, and extra control protocols into an IGP with Segment Routing extensions.

questions.q: A brownfield customer says the MPLS WAN already works. Which problem can still justify a Segment Routing conversation?
choices: Operational complexity, slow change, and difficult troubleshooting even though traffic is flowing
questions.why: The activity answer says a working network can still be costly to operate, troubleshoot, and change.

questions.q: A retailer with about 150 branches, mixed MPLS and broadband, and growing SaaS is pointed toward which WAN direction in the module wrap-up?
choices: A single Layer 2 domain across all countries
SD-WAN, so policy can use both transports and send cloud traffic on a better path
questions.why: The growing-retail scenario is the SD-WAN example: many branches, mixed transports, and cloud applications.

questions.q: Why has the branch router become a larger enforcement point?
choices: MPLS labels replaced the need for policy
All SaaS traffic is now unencrypted
Local Internet breakout bypasses the central security stack, and IoT plus encrypted traffic reduce visibility
Branch routers no longer forward packets
questions.why: Direct Internet, cloud access, guests, and unmanaged devices show up first at the WAN edge. The router has to segment, enforce, and export telemetry.

questions.q: Cisco Secure Boot checks the boot chain using which hardware root?
questions.why: The secure-boot sequence starts at the Trust Anchor, which checks the microloader, bootloader, and operating system before the image is trusted.

questions.q: Zone-based firewall policy on a router is applied between what?
choices: Security zones, using class maps to match traffic and policy maps to pass, inspect, or drop it
questions.why: The operation slide is class-map, policy-map, then zone-pair. Zones are applied to interfaces.

questions.q: Enterprise firewall with application awareness adds which recognition to ZBFW?
choices: NBAR recognition of more than 1,500 Layer 7 applications
questions.why: NBAR lets the router allow or block by application, category, family, or group rather than only ports.

questions.q: The router next-generation firewall in this module combines application-aware ZBFW with which engine?
choices: Unified Threat Defense, including IPS, malware protection, and URL filtering
questions.why: UTD adds Snort IPS, AMP, URL filtering, TLS decryption, and identity-aware policy.

questions.q: Snort signature sets on the router are described as which three postures?
choices: Connectivity over security, balanced, and security over connectivity
questions.why: Those three signature-set levels trade inspection depth against connectivity. Talos updates can be pushed by the SD-WAN Manager.

questions.q: A URL reputation score of 90 is classified as what?
questions.why: The BrightCloud scale is 1–20 high risk, 21–40 suspicious, 41–60 moderate, 61–80 low risk, and 81–100 trustworthy.

questions.q: Why does the TLS proxy discussion matter on a branch router?
choices: TLS removed the need for any firewall
More than 90 percent of Internet traffic is encrypted, so inspection needs a controlled decrypt and has a performance cost
Decryption makes the router faster in every case
questions.why: The slide says malware hides in encrypted traffic and selective decryption is the practical compromise.

questions.q: Advanced malware protection on the router is described as using which functions?
choices: File reputation, retrospection, and analysis through Cisco Malware Analytics
questions.why: AMP covers reputation and retrospection, with Threat Grid analysis, on protocols such as HTTP and SMTP when decryption is available.

questions.q: WAN MACsec is positioned for which outcome?
choices: Line-rate Layer 2 encryption over public Ethernet transport, including multipoint topologies
questions.why: WAN MACsec extends 802.1AE across carrier Ethernet for high-speed links such as data-center interconnect, at line rate.

questions.q: Security Service Edge is best described as what?
choices: Cloud-delivered security for web, cloud services, and private applications
questions.why: SSE is delivered primarily from the cloud and typically includes secure web gateway, CASB, and zero trust network access functions.

questions.q: A cloud-delivered firewall, or firewall-as-a-service, adds which coverage beyond a secure web gateway?
choices: Layer 3 and 4 controls and non-web Internet access, plus IPS and application control
questions.why: The CDFW picture shows ports 80 and 443 on the secure web gateway and non-web traffic handled by the cloud firewall.

questions.q: Which functions does the course list for a secure web gateway?
choices: URL filtering, reputation, TLS inspection, malware sandboxing, and remote browser isolation
questions.why: The SWG slide stacks those web-security controls in the cloud proxy path.

questions.q: Why is full SSL decryption called out as an operational concern?
choices: It is required on every packet or the proxy fails closed with no alternative
It removes malware with no performance cost
It is resource intensive, so it should be applied selectively
questions.why: The SWG performance slide says decryption is expensive. The router TLS discussion makes the same point about selective decryption.

questions.q: A CASB tenant control is used to do what?
choices: Allow the corporate Microsoft 365 instance and block personal instances
questions.why: The example distinguishes the corporate tenant from personal tenants and can limit the choice to groups of users.

questions.q: CASB discovery of third-party apps is aimed at which problem?
choices: OAuth grants that let unreviewed extensions into the Microsoft 365 tenant
questions.why: The slide covers visibility into third-party applications and plug-ins granted access through OAuth.

questions.q: Zero Trust Network Access replaces a full-tunnel VPN with what?
choices: Unrestricted access to the whole private network
A Layer 2 broadcast domain for remote users
A shared pre-shared key for every application
Per-application access after the user, device, and context are checked
questions.why: ZTNA verifies identity and context, then opens only the approved application. It can be client-based or clientless.

questions.q: Why is DNS-layer security described as an early control?
choices: DNS only works for data-center servers
DNS is the first step for almost every Internet connection, before the file runs or the IP session starts
DNS cannot be answered with a block page
questions.why: The slide says a safe request returns the real address and a malicious request can return a block page.

questions.q: How do the two DLP deployment methods differ?
choices: API DLP blocks non-web traffic at Layer 4
Real-time DLP inspects web traffic in the secure web gateway; API DLP inspects sanctioned SaaS through cloud APIs
Both methods only scan tape backups
Real-time DLP cannot see unsanctioned applications
questions.why: Inline SWG DLP covers sanctioned and unsanctioned web use. API DLP is for data already in the cloud application.

questions.q: Remote browser isolation protects the endpoint by doing what?
choices: Running the web session in a cloud browser and streaming a rendered result so active content does not execute locally
Caching every file on the laptop
questions.why: RBI is for risky or unknown sites. The user sees rendered content instead of running the site’s code.
